summary: Ten comment-endorsed finds spanning developer tools, search, programming resources, games, and physical products.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 prior-day front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: 98.css
items.source_story_title: A browser-native classic Visual Basic VB6 IDE
items.summary: CSS library for Windows 98-style interfaces; praised as a personal-project foundation.
items.why_included: Direct first-hand praise connects a concrete library to repeated personal-project use.
items.evidence: HanClinto uses 98.css for many personal projects and calls it great and refreshing.

evidence_sources.author: HanClinto
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using 98.css [0] as a foundation for building many of my personal projects lately -- I think it's pretty great, and a really refreshing return to some older paradigms.

items.name: mold
items.source_story_title: Mold Linker Version 3.0.0 Release – Rewritten in Rust
items.summary: Fast linker; a distro builder reports substantial speed advantages over LLVM's lld.
items.why_included: A production user independently endorses the story subject with a concrete speed comparison.
items.evidence: lrvick says their distro switched from lld to mold because lld was much slower; the same comment warns that building Rust dependencies delays those gains.

evidence_sources.author: lrvick
evidence_sources.excerpt: LLD would work fine for the whole tree, and did previously, but is much much slower than mold which is why we switched to mold. Having to build all dependencies of rust including python and openssl and everything else before being able to use mold erases most of the full-tree build speedups as the path to rust is already about 80% of the full tree build time.

items.name: CHICKEN Scheme
items.source_story_title: Interview with Chicken Scheme Maintainer Sjamaan/Peter Bex
items.summary: Scheme-to-C compiler; a longtime user praises its approachable foreign-function interface.
items.why_included: Years of positive first-hand use provide stronger evidence than language nostalgia.
items.evidence: jrapdx3 describes several years with CHICKEN as gratifying and credits its easy, sensible FFI.

evidence_sources.author: jrapdx3
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've used Chicken Scheme for a few years. For the most part, it's been a gratifying experience. For me, Chicken's easy to use and sensible FFI is big part of the reason.

items.name: Serper

items.evidence: sejje says they used Serper's free allowance and found it good.

evidence_sources.author: sejje

items.name: SearXNG

evidence_sources.author: laumars

items.evidence: Keegs calls the book a great algorithms reference and interview-preparation resource.

items.name: SQL Doom
items.source_story_title: We ported the original Doom to SQL
items.summary: Doom implemented in SQL; admired for turning query planning into a state machine.
items.why_included: A playful but explicit endorsement makes this a concrete systems rabbit hole.
items.evidence: soltanov admires the port's use of query planning as a state machine and says they love it.

evidence_sources.author: soltanov
evidence_sources.excerpt: Less lines of code than vanilla C while abusing query planning as a state machine is peak engineering malpractice. I love it.

items.name: Mack's Flightguard
items.source_story_title: The first fully implanted cochlear implant reaches patients
items.summary: Reusable earplugs with a carry case; praised for making everyday use convenient.
items.why_included: The exact linked product resolves to a named earplug with concrete first-hand praise.
items.evidence: schiffern praises the earplugs and especially the pocket-sized case for keeping them available throughout the day.

evidence_sources.author: schiffern
evidence_sources.excerpt: The special part isn't the earplugs (and they're good!), the special part is the little carry case so they can live in my pocket 24/7.

items.name: Foscarini Le Soleil
items.summary: Sculptural pendant lamp; praised for asymmetrical layers and exceptional light distribution.
items.why_included: A reply supplies an explicit named favorite outside the submitted article's lamp collection.
items.evidence: eps names Le Soleil as a recent favorite and praises its asymmetry, suspended layers, and light distribution.

evidence_sources.author: eps
evidence_sources.excerpt: One of my recent favourites - Le Soleil by Foscarini - https://www.foscarini.com/en/product/le-soleil-std-s-en/ It's wonderfully asymmetrical without overdoing it, with every layer suspended and swaying independently when prodded. Exceptional light distribution.
